title: CTSS and the Birth of Time-Sharing (1961)
explainer: The idea that a scheduler should interleave many users' work on one machine, giving each the illusion of a personal computer, began with Fernando Corbato's Compatible Time-Sharing System at MIT, first demonstrated in 1961 on a modified IBM 709. CTSS's success in showing that interactive, multi-user scheduling was practical led directly to Project MAC and Multics - the system whose complexity Unix itself was later a reaction against.

title: Erlang and the Mathematics of Queueing (1909)
explainer: Every scheduler is, underneath, managing a queue, and the mathematics for reasoning about waiting lines - how long tasks wait, how utilization relates to delay - originated with Agner Krarup Erlang's 1909 analysis of telephone traffic at the Copenhagen Telephone Company, where he showed random call arrivals follow a Poisson process. The queueing theory he founded still underlies how scheduler and network throughput and latency are analyzed today.
